explanation: Deduplicate values in a set. Remove one value and consume every consecutive neighbor on both sides. Each distinct value is removed once, so all runs together take linear expected time.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The set contains exactly the values not yet assigned to a processed consecutive component. Expanding downward and upward consumes the entire component containing the chosen value. Components are disjoint, so their sizes cover every candidate interval and the greatest size is optimal.
walkthrough: For [8,3,5,4,20,5], duplicates disappear in the set. Expanding from 3 consumes 4 and 5, giving a run of length 3. The isolated values 8 and 20 cannot improve it.
edgeCases: Duplicate input values do not increase interval length.
Neighbor arithmetic is widened to avoid wrapping int.MinValue to int.MaxValue.
